result.reason: I found nothing that kills the idea, but it is weak. result.killer: The market is much smaller than the claim says, and it is the wrong buyer group. Only exporters (in practice avocado packer-exporters) apply for the CLA on the free STPS VELAGRO platform. VELAGRO checks compliance automatically against IMSS and confirms the certificate against the export pedimento through VUCEM. Orchards, cutting-crew firms and packers that don't export do not file. They only have to stay current on their IMSS and REPSE duties, which existing payroll tools already handle. APEAM reported 74 packers in Michoacán in 2022, and Jalisco had 11 certified packhouses as of August 2026, so there are roughly 85 to 100 filers, most of them mid-sized or large. result.reason: The idea is not killed by a competitor, since no private VELAGRO software or consultancy turned up. It fails on who the buyer is and how many there are. IDC (2 Oct 2026) and the pilot coverage say the exporter registers its value chain and applies, while producers, cutting firms and packers don't request their own certificate during the pilot. That leaves about 85 to 100 avocado packer-exporters, and many are large or foreign-owned, not small firms. Compliance data comes straight from IMSS, so there is little left for a tool to compile. During the pilot, not having a CLA doesn't stop shipments. Upside: berries and other crops are planned but have no published rules yet, and the 2027 employer-registration phase could add work for the chain. Sanctions and renewal frequency remain unverified.

result.competitor: Free IMSS ICSOE portal with an official bulk CSV template and guide (imss.gob.mx/icsoe). Paid SISUB/ICSOE CSV templates and courses from elconta.mx. Training from COFIDE. result.duty: LSS art. 15-A (ICSOE, IMSS): REPSE-registered contractors file a four-monthly information return per contract, due by the 17th of Jan, May and Sep. Penalty: LSS art. 304-A fr. XXII and 304-B fr. V, 500-2,000 UMA. No fine applies if the filer corrects late of their own accord before IMSS acts (art. 304-C). SISUB: Ley INFONAVIT art. 29 Bis, same calendar. Rule texts were seen on the mley.mx and sdv.com.mx compendia, not in the DOF itself.
result.market: No official count of active REPSE registrants found. STPS cancelled more than 51,000 REPSE registrations in 2025, and more than 13,000 firms re-registered (Tiempo, 30 Sep 2026). A commercial guide cites more than 71,000 registered by Sep 2021. In 2024 only about 53% of firms due for renewal re-qualified (IDC Online). This suggests tens of thousands of active filers, but the figure is unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. LSS art. 15-A requires REPSE contractors to file the ICSOE every four months, by 17 Jan, 17 May and 17 Sep. Missing or late filing is fined 500-2,000 UMA under LSS art. 304-A XXII and 304-B V. SISUB under Ley INFONAVIT art. 29 Bis follows the same calendar. I found no dedicated software that generates or validates ICSOE/SISUB files. What exists is the free IMSS portal with a bulk CSV template, CSV templates sold by elconta.mx, consultancies and courses. I could not check whether payroll suites (CONTPAQi, Runa) export these files. The market is large: STPS cancelled more than 51k REPSE registrations in 2025. But the free CSV template means low pain, payroll bureaus already absorb the work, and the job is three short filings a year. Willingness to pay is weak.

result.competitor: SICAR (sicar.mx), a Mexican point-of-sale system with a pharmacy edition, already covers the core recording job. Its pharmacy page says it automatically generates sales reports for antibiotics and controlled medicines with doctor and prescription data, "listos para presentarse ante las autoridades". It requires the doctor's name and cédula profesional for every controlled sale, records prescription folios, and claims its reports meet COFEPRIS rules. Price: MXN 4,940 one-time for the server licence and MXN 1,320 per terminal. A 2010 trade report said 7 in 10 pharmacies already used software to capture antibiotic sales data. A 2021 BUAP thesis built a point-of-sale prototype for the same job. The authorised book itself still appears to be paper, so a separate product could only offer printing or transcribing the book and preparing the paper previsiones forms. That is a thin add-on to point-of-sale systems pharmacies already use. I could only run a few competitor searches, so other pharmacy point-of-sale vendors were not checked.
result.duty: Real, but only partly confirmed from secondary sources. Pharmacies, droguerías and boticas that sell estupefacientes or psicotrópicos must keep authorised control books (COFEPRIS-03-005, free, resolved in 5 working days). The Coahuila RETyS listing says the books must be presented as originals, in person. They must also file the previsiones de compra-venta notice (COFEPRIS-03-014). The Coahuila listing says this notice is due every 6 months and carries a fee, and it is filed in person. The Zacatecas listing gives no frequency, says the procedure is free and gives 1 year as the resolution period. Both listings are on papelea.com, a third-party site. I did not reach an official gob.mx or COFEPRIS page. I found no penalty amounts. Retaining prescriptions and recording antibiotic sales (doctor name, cédula profesional, quantity) has been required since 2010. I did not find evidence that electronic books are accepted; the sources point to paper books, presented in person.
result.market: No national count found. The only figure is from Salud y Fármacos: one state (not named, undated) had 2,962 pharmacies selling controlled medicines. A 2015 Salud y Fármacos note put Jalisco at about 8,000 pharmacy establishments. Nationally, pharmacies number in the tens of thousands (an estimate, not a sourced figure), but the share holding a controlled-medicine licence is unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real but light. The previsiones notice is twice a year according to one state listing, and the book permit is free, quick and filed on paper. The heavier day-to-day work is recording each controlled or antibiotic sale with doctor data, and SICAR, an established Mexican point-of-sale system, already does this with reports it says are ready to give to the authorities. A 2010 report said most pharmacies already used software for antibiotic records. Electronic books do not appear to be accepted, so a new product could not replace the authorised paper book; it would be a feature of point-of-sale systems pharmacies already own. Willingness to pay for a separate tool is low.

result.duty: Two rules in force. (1) SADER phytosanitary agreement, DOF 1 Oct 2026, effective 2 Oct 2026, tied to the NOM-066-FITO-1995 change: fruit exported to the US must come only from certified orchards registered in SITAEX, supplied directly to the packer, with collectors, traders and maquiladores banned. SITAEX holds the orchard registry, harvest estimates and phytosanitary status. The press says it starts 31 December (year not stated, presumably 2026). (2) SAT criterion 60/ISR/N in Anexo 7 RMF 2026, in the Third Resolution of Modifications, effective 31 Dec 2026. Packer purchases are deductible only if the packer verifies certified origin and direct supply, keeps documents proving compliance with the SADER agreement, and holds a CFDI issued by the orchard's possessor, usufructuary or owner. The penalty is losing the ISR deduction under LISR art. 27-I. In the agreement, a quarantine pest finding means the shipment is returned or destroyed. The SAT text names no other sanctions, and I did not read the full DOF text of the SADER agreement. The duty is continuous, applying to every purchase.
result.market: Small. APEAM had 74 packers in Michoacán in 2022 (portalfruticola). Jalisco had 11 certified packhouses, 609 orchards and 227 producers in Aug 2026. Berdegué said 75% of Michoacán packers are enabled for export, without an absolute number. That suggests roughly 80-120 export packers, many of them mid-size or large. Michoacán had more than 30,000 producers (2022), and these orchard owners must issue CFDIs, which is a larger but low-paying secondary segment. I did not open the SENASICA SRRC directory to count it.
result.reason: The duty is real. SADER's agreement was published in the DOF on 1 Oct 2026 and took effect 2 Oct. It requires export fruit to come only from certified orchards registered in SITAEX, supplied directly, with no collectors or maquila. SAT criterion 60/ISR/N (Tercera Resolución de Modificaciones RMF 2026, effective 31 Dec 2026) makes purchases non-deductible unless the packer can show this compliance and holds a CFDI from the orchard owner. No vendor sells a tool for the CFDI-to-certified-orchard check. General produce ERPs (BatchMaster at Global Frut, Reserva ERP) and the state's own SITAEX may cover much of it. The market is small and fairly sophisticated: roughly 74 Michoacán packers (2022 figure) plus 11 in Jalisco.

result.competitor: No software or app for preparing the regularisation file was found in Spanish searches. Alternatives are free orientation at CONAGUA local offices (for example SLP, and earlier Jalisco modules), law firms (Garrigues, Holland & Knight, Basham, HLC) and gestoría blogs such as noticiasgobierno.com. For the meter side, CONAGUA-approved service providers (PSIs) and verification units (UVs) under NMX-AA-179 already supply meters, and the norm includes a data-transmission procedure to CONAGUA. result.duty: Acuerdo for the first stage of regularisation of concession and assignment titles (DOF 15 Jul 2026, CONAGUA). Legal basis: 6th transitory of the Ley General de Aguas decree (DOF 11 Dec 2025). It covers titles that expired between 1 Jan 2009 and 16 Jul 2026 without a timely extension request. Covered uses are domestic, public urban, agricultural, livestock and aquaculture; agroindustrial use is excluded. Ejidos, irrigation districts and irrigation units have no volume cap; individuals are capped at 1 million m3 a year. The window runs 16 Jul 2026 to 15 Jul 2027 (365 days). Holland & Knight lists these requirements: installed meter, fees paid for the last 5 fiscal years, works operating for 2 years, no sanction proceedings pending. The accord has 13 requirements in total; only 4 were seen. CONAGUA will check actual volume use over 2 years and may cut the concession volume to what is actually used. The penalty is indirect: an expired title means operating without a concession, which risks extinction or closure (the closure claim comes from a low-quality blog). The meter duty (NMX-AA-179, deadline 1 Jul 2022) comes from the Ley Federal de Derechos rules (DOF 9 Apr 2020). Not confirmed: the 90-day appearance period, third-party filing, telemetry rules for 2026, and the full DOF text (not fetched).
result.market: No national count of eligible expired titles was found. CONAGUA says only that "a significant number" of titles remain unregularised after the 2014-2025 decrees. Regional figures: about 400 expired wells in La Laguna (El Siglo de Torreón, 2026; page blocked with a 403, title only) and about 7,000 wells without a title or not in use in Chihuahua (El Congresista). The eligible pool is likely thousands to tens of thousands of titles, but this is unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real. CONAGUA's first-phase regularisation accord was published in the DOF on 15 Jul 2026 under the 6th transitory of the Ley General de Aguas, and it is in force from 16 Jul 2026 to 15 Jul 2027. It needs an installed meter, 5 years of fees paid, works operating for 2 years and no sanction proceedings. I found no software doing this core job. However, it is a one-off, year-long window, not a recurring duty. Local CONAGUA offices give free guidance, and buyers are low-digital farmers and ejidos. Meter work (NMX-AA-179, with transmission to CONAGUA) already belongs to approved service providers (PSIs). I found no count of eligible titles; only 400 wells in La Laguna is reported. This suits a done-for-you service more than a SaaS.

result.duty: NOM-033-FITO-1995 (DOF 24/06/1996) is in force. It requires anyone who sells agricultural pesticides to file an aviso de inicio de funcionamiento, appoint a technical manager (agronomist) responsible for use recommendations, and get certified, with assessments that can be done by a Tercero Especialista Autorizado (SENASICA directrices, June 2022). It also bans expired, banned, adulterated, bulk or repackaged products and requires sales control for products that need a written recommendation. SENASICA posters still promote certification. Not confirmed from the primary text, because the PDFs could not be read: how often the sales log must be kept, the claim that a supplier list goes to SENASICA every 2 years, how often certificates are renewed, and the specific penalties (presumably under the Ley Federal de Sanidad Vegetal).
result.market: Not found. No published count of certified or notified pesticide sellers was located. SENASICA keeps a Directorio Fitosanitario and state representation offices, but no total figure was found. A transparency request (PNT) would be needed. This is unverifiable for now.
result.reason: The duty is real and current. NOM-033-FITO-1995 (DOF 24/06/1996, under Article 37 bis of the Ley Federal de Sanidad Vegetal) requires an aviso de inicio de funcionamiento, a named technical manager, and certification through a TEA (directrices from June 2022). It also requires sales control for products that need a written recommendation. No Mexican software built for this was found, only generic or foreign agro-input inventory tools such as Agroinventario (Chile, not available in Mexico). Weaknesses: the core job is a paper sales log, which ordinary POS software can largely handle. Enforcement intensity, the 2-year supplier list, renewal frequency and the size of the market could not be confirmed. Shops are rural and fragmented, and are likely to pay little.

result.competitor: I found no commercial UMA or cintillo software in Mexico. The nearest foreign analogues are HAMS (Scotland and Ireland) and GMS deer-management software (US). Free state channels exist: Coahuila accepts the report online at sma.gob.mx/tramites-vida-silvestre and lists a vidasilvestre.sma.gob.mx system, and SEMARNAT runs the federal trámite. In practice, consultant responsables técnicos registered with SEMARNAT prepare the management plans and reports. I could not confirm whether SEMARNAT runs a national electronic UMA or tag platform.
result.duty: Reglamento LGVS art. 50 requires a yearly activity report filed April to June, covering indicators, harvest results, hunting-service provider licence numbers and socio-economic data, on form FF-SEMARNAT-099, free of charge. Contingency reports are due within 3 working days. Art. 52 sets the sanctions for omission: a written warning or denial of harvest authorizations on the first omission, and revocation of the UMA registration after 2 consecutive years. According to a UAM document, reviewers check SINAT by RFC to confirm the annual report was filed before processing other requests. I did not verify the 30-day report that hunting-service providers must file after each service on public land.
result.market: Nuevo León has 2,757 registered UMA ranches (state congress, 2023). Northern Coahuila has up to about 800 hunting ranches. Chihuahua has about 250 hunting UMAs according to the claim's source, which I did not re-check. Nationally there were about 5,000 UMAs in 2002 (INE/SEMARNAT), and an academic study reports the number declining between 1999 and 2021. I could not open the datos.gob.mx dataset (HTTP 403), so I have no current national total. My estimate is a few thousand hunting UMAs, mostly in the north.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. Under Reglamento LGVS art. 50 every UMA files an annual activity report between April and June (form FF-SEMARNAT-099), plus contingency reports within 3 working days. Art. 52 sanctions a missed report with a written warning or denial of harvest authorizations on first omission, and revocation of registration after two consecutive years. I found no software for UMA reports or tag (cintillo) management. Even so, the opportunity is weak. The report is one free annual form, filed online through state or SEMARNAT portals (Coahuila's sma.gob.mx). In practice the responsable técnico (consultant biologists) usually prepares it, so the buyer group is small and fragmented. Willingness to pay is low, and the market is seasonal and only a few thousand UMAs.

result.competitor: I found no commercial Mexican veterinary software that advertises quantified recetas with folios or the monthly Group I report. Comparasoftware and AgendaPro list only general clinic-management tools, and I did not check each vendor. The main threat is the state's own system: SENASICA's Sistema Informático de Trazabilidad de Productos Veterinarios (SITPV). Phase 1 counts each receta by folio, records species, weight and number of animals, and holds a database of all Group I products and antibiotics. Mexico presented it at WOAH Americas in Dec 2024 and again in Nov 2025 ("Sistema de prescripción electrónica México"). I could not confirm whether it is live; both PDFs are image-only. Argentina's SENASA made electronic prescriptions mandatory in July 2026 (Res. 654/2026), which suggests the region is moving toward free state systems.
result.duty: Confirmed and in force. NOM-064-ZOO-2000 sets how veterinary drugs are classified and prescribed, and applies to everyone who prescribes, sells or uses them. A Group I product needs a receta médica cuantificada with a consecutive folio authorised by SADER/SENASICA, printed as an original plus one copy. The establishment that fills it keeps the original for 1 year. The MVZ files monthly Group I use reports (Excel by email) and keeps the Anexo 5 control format, which records folio, registration, batch, species, dose and withdrawal period. To get a permanent key (CPA) and folios, the MVZ applies to the state representation, which authorises 50 folios at a time and is slow to respond. A February 2025 SENASICA alert (Ketamin-Pet) shows the folio requirement is still being enforced. Penalties fall under the Ley Federal de Sanidad Animal, but I did not confirm the amounts. I did not confirm whether NOM-064 is being revised. SENASICA's open-data list of Group I products was updated on 2026-03-11.
result.market: Not found. I did not reach a count of MVZs holding a CPA and folios, or a register of vet pharmacies and distributors. The only figure is the 30% monthly reporting rate in 2023, with no total behind it. Group I covers controlled drugs such as ketamine and some hormones and antibiotics, so the users are mostly livestock vets and vet pharmacies. My rough guess is a few thousand to low tens of thousands nationally; this is unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real. Under NOM-064-ZOO-2000, Group I products need a receta cuantificada with folios that SADER/SENASICA authorises. The seller keeps the original for 1 year, and the vet (MVZ) sends a monthly Group I report as an Excel file by email. Compliance is weak: in 2023 only 30% of MVZs filed regularly, so enforcement is soft and willingness to pay is low. SENASICA is building its own free electronic prescription system, SITPV, presented at WOAH in Dec 2024 and Nov 2025. Its live status is unconfirmed, and if it launches it removes the gap. The folios are a state-controlled resource, so the product depends on state processes. I found no commercial vendor that covers this. I could not find how many MVZs hold folios.

result.competitor: I found no Mexican product that prepares or keeps DGSP Registro Nacional filings. Generic guard-operations software (GuardsPro/Guardso, CGuardPro, OfficerReports) covers patrols, shifts and incident reports and does not mention the DGSP or the Registro. Not reached: whether the DGSP/SSPC runs an online filing portal (the Reglamento allows electronic or printed forms), and Mexican payroll/HR vendors for guard companies that may export DGSP formats. Both are risks to check.
result.duty: LFSP art. 32 (prestador obligations) and Reglamento arts. 32-34: register altas/bajas with the cause, plus uniforms, vehicles, arms and radios, in the Registro Nacional de Empresas, Personal y Equipo de Seguridad Privada, on electronic or printed forms. Operational staff need annual medical, psychological and toxicology exams. Written notices are due within 3 business days for theft or loss of documents or IDs and for suspension of activities, and within 5 for asset-disposal orders. Firms must tell the state authority about a federal authorisation within 30 days. Modality VI firms file a buyer registry every 6 months. Altas/bajas have no fixed deadline, so they are event-driven. Penalties under LFSP art. 42 run from amonestación to fines and suspension or revocation. Enforcement is current: DGSP file DGSP/DELC/PAS/169/2026 (28 Aug 2026) gave GCH Seguridad Privada an amonestación for not reporting the baja of 112 uniforms. I could not verify the claim's 1,000 UMA fine. I found no source showing that a Ley General de Seguridad Privada has been published. A Senate bill passed in 2018, but nothing confirms it was enacted, so the LFSP still applies.
result.market: I found no official 2025/2026 count. A commercial training site claims about 8,500 authorised firms employing more than 600,000 guards, citing the Registro Nacional; this is unofficial. Jalisco: 289 firms, 83 of them state-authorised (nmas.com.mx, date unclear). The DGSP open-data list of federally authorised firms was last updated in Oct 2018 and gives no total on the page. Each of the 32 states also licenses single-state firms under its own law, for example Nuevo León and Estado de México.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force under the Ley Federal de Seguridad Privada (last reformed in 2011) and its Reglamento. Firms must record personnel altas/bajas with the cause, uniforms, vehicles, arms and radios in the Registro Nacional, and give operational staff annual medical, psychological and toxicology exams. The DGSP enforces it: in Aug 2026 GCH Seguridad Privada received a public amonestación for not reporting the baja of 112 uniforms. Weaknesses: the rules set no fixed deadline for altas/bajas, so the work is event-driven, and the sanction I verified was a warning, not a fine. I found no DGSP-specific Mexican software. Generic guard tools (GuardsPro, CGuardPro) don't cover the Registro. I couldn't confirm whether the DGSP has an online filing portal. The market of about 8,500 firms is an unofficial figure.

result.competitor: The free official STPS VELAGRO platform does the filing. No private software, consultancy or service built for VELAGRO/CLA was found in searches. Possible entrants are generic REPSE/IMSS payroll providers and APEAM, the packers' association, which co-designed the scheme. Unverified whether any of them already covers the chain-data job.
result.duty: CLA through the STPS VELAGRO platform (Lineamientos and Acuerdo Técnico, DOF 15 Sep 2026; SE-STPS tariff acuerdo, DOF 1 Oct 2026, which recognises CLAs issued since 15 Sep). The exporter applies with e.firma, gives 12 months of statistics, registers the value chain (1-7 Nov 2026), then adds IMSS patronal registrations monthly from Jan 2027 (first 7 days of each month). The technical factor phases in from May 2027 and the permanent regime starts Feb 2028. The CLA is renewed per validity period (applications up to 7 days before expiry) and declared in the export pedimento. Without a valid CLA, exports cannot continue. Neither the DOF acuerdo nor the IDC article names explicit sanctions. Only avocado is covered for now; berries are announced but undated.
result.market: APEAM figures: about 30,000 producers, 42,000-54,000 orchards, and 74 to more than 90 packing houses in Michoacán (figures vary by date). Jalisco had 11 certified packers in 2022. The STPS cites more than 18,000 avocado cutters and packers not affiliated to IMSS. The direct CLA applicants number roughly 100+ packers/exporters. The wider affected base is the cutting crews and the producers with 5 ha or more; their number was not found.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. The STPS Acuerdo Técnico (signed 15 Sep 2026) puts avocado (FA 0804.40.01) under the CLA, based on LFT art. 283 Quáter. The covered parties are producers with 5 ha or more, cutting firms (must hold REPSE), packers and exporters. IMSS registro patronal coverage rises 25/50/75/100% from 2027, and certificates are renewed in cycles. The formal filers are only about 90 to 100 packers/exporters, mostly mid-size; the pain sits in collecting chain data from thousands of orchards and crews. No private software or VELAGRO service was found. The pilot rules keep changing, APEAM or payroll/REPSE vendors could add this, and the official texts name no sanctions. Berries are planned but have no date.

Duty is real: LISR art. 82 fr. VI, RMF ficha 21/ISR, and the transparency declaration is due in May. In 2023, 699 donatarias missed it, and missing it is grounds for losing authorisation. The CFDI donatarias complement and electronic accounting also apply. SAT counts 10,017 donatarias in 2026, down from 10,361 in 2025. Most are small, but the whole market is only about 10k, mostly CDMX. Competition: SAT's free "Transparencia" program covers the declaration. The searches found no Mexican donataria-specific tool, but generic PACs and accounting suites (Aspel, CONTPAQi) likely include the complement. Buying runs through accountants, and small charities have little money to pay. Two checks are open: PLD duties, and fines of about 102k pesos, which come from 2022 sources. The score stays low because of the small market and the overlap with generic accounting.

result.competitor: No dedicated ICSOE/SISUB software found. Consultancies (Praxium), training, and the free IMSS/Infonavit portals. Payroll-suite export unconfirmed.
result.duty: LSS art. 15-A and Ley INFONAVIT art. 29 Bis: ICSOE and SISUB due 17 Jan, May and Sep for the preceding four months, including nil filings. Fine 500-2,000 UMA under LSS 304-A XXII and 304-B V.
result.market: No official count of active REPSE registrants found; sources say only "thousands". Unverified.
result.reason: Duty is real: ICSOE (IMSS) and SISUB (Infonavit) are due by 17 Jan, May and Sep, and "no information" filings are also required. The fine is 500-2,000 UMA (LSS arts. 304-A XXII and 304-B V), about 58.7k-234.6k MXN at UMA 2026 of 117.31. The Infonavit fine is reported as 3-350 UMA. These figures come from consultancy sources, not the IMSS or Infonavit. I found no dedicated filer or checker software. I could not confirm whether CONTPAQi Nóminas or Aspel NOI export ICSOE/SISUB; nothing says they do. Free IMSS and Infonavit portals take the filings. The REPSE registrant count was not found. The pain is moderate and the filing is only three times a year. Consultancies already sell this at low prices, and the buyer is a small contractor, so willingness to pay is limited. Overlaps K03.

result.duty: Controlled-drug control books must be authorised (COFEPRIS-03-005) and kept. A previsiones notice is filed under COFEPRIS-03-014, said to be semiannual, with 03-004 annual. Antibiotic prescription retention has applied since 2010. Official text and penalties were not verified.
result.market: Not found. A 2015 Salud y Fármacos bulletin cites 2,962 pharmacies selling narcotics or controlled drugs, state unclear.
result.reason: Duty is plausible: COFEPRIS-03-005 (control-book permit, free, about 5 working days) and 03-014 (previsiones notice, one aggregator says every six months) exist, and COFEPRIS checks that authorised control books exist. Only secondary aggregators were found. The 03-014 frequency conflicts (another ficha shows a 1-year resolution time), the 2026 reform effect was not checked, and the penalty was not found. An IMSS tender annex mentions books that are written or electronic, authorised by the health authority, so software is possibly allowed. No dedicated Mexican compliance product turned up, but I did not check pharmacy POS vendors by name. Market: no count of licensed pharmacies; one 2015 state figure was 2,962 pharmacies selling controlled drugs, state unclear. Pain is modest, filings are infrequent, and the buyers are fragmented.

The duty is real. A CNE acuerdo (DOF 21-Jan-2026) binds permit holders selling LP gas to end users (plant, autotanque, delivery vehicle, retail stations). They must respect weekly maximum prices, report transaction volumes, and supply information the CNE requests, or face unspecified sanctions (Cuatrecasas note only; I did not see the DOF text). The workflow is thin. The CNE publishes the prices itself, so there is nothing to compute or file beyond volume reporting. A Milenio snippet says the CNE dropped the cap for final sale at bodegas and service stations in Nov 2025 (acuerdo A/023/2022 partly repealed). I could not open that page to confirm it, and the Jan 2026 note appears to contradict it. No competitor or vendor search found anything. No current permit count was found; the datos.gob.mx CNE CSVs would give one. Weak standalone product; at best a feature of LP gas ERP or volumetric-control software (K26).

Art. 83 is in the Reglamento de la LFAFE, not the Ley itself. It requires every general-permit holder (fabricantes and talleres, comerciantes, others) to file a report with SEDENA in the first 10 days of each month on the previous month's operations. The fabricante and comerciante categories can cover pyrotechnics, although the text mentions only arms serial numbers. I did not find the penalty, whether filing is paper or electronic, or any competing software. The only online SEDENA channel I found is VUCEM, which handles foreign-trade procedures. Market is small and informal: roughly 436 to 680 permits in Tultepec, with about 50% of workshops reported clandestine. The buyers are hard to reach and unlikely to pay, so the score stays low.

Duty is real: CNBV instructivos for R08 (Dec 2021 version) and R24-B (Dec 2023 version) exist, and filing goes via SITI under Circular Única art. 310. I did not confirm penalties or frequency from primary text. Market is small: one study citing CNBV reports gives about 153 supervised SOCAPs in 2022. I found no 2025-26 count. Competition was not resolved: searches found no named vendors, but core-banking vendors for SOCAPs probably include regulatory reports in the core. The buyer pool of about 150 entities is small, many are served by federations, and the reports are generated from the core system. Hence a low score.

Duty is real: LFCPQ art. 7 requires annual reports to COFEPRIS (identity, counterparties, volumes per activity, proof that activity matches corporate purpose and import/export permits). The article gives no due date or penalty; art. 23 may carry sanctions but I did not read it. The 2023 reform created the SISUS electronic system and filings go through VUCEM, so a state portal already exists. SAT Anexo 10 RGCE 2026 lists Sector 3 (precursors and essential chemicals) in the PISE. I found no commercial software and no counts of firms. Market is niche and probably served by customs brokers and sanitary consultants. Competition and market size were not checked. Score stays at 3.

The duty is real. Criterio 60/ISR/N (Tercera Resolución de Modificaciones a la RMF 2026, Anexo 7) makes avocado purchases for export deductible only if the fruit comes direct from certified orchards, the CFDI is issued by the owner, usufructuary or possessor, and the packer keeps compliance documents. It takes effect 31 Dec 2026, and the phytosanitary agreement was published in the DOF on 1 Oct 2026. The penalty is loss of the ISR deduction, with no fines described. The duty is one-off at start-up, then ongoing per purchase. Market is small: about 72 certified Michoacán packers (2021-22) and about 49,000 certified orchards. The sources do not give a current total of packers, so that figure may be out of date. Big packers likely have in-house systems. SITAEX is a state system and may absorb the traceability function. Packers are a thin, reachable niche, but the product is narrow. I did not find a dedicated competitor, though I ran only a limited search. The official DOF text was not reached.

Duty is real: IMSS agreement ACDO.AS1.HCT.270126/7.P.DIR (DOF 9-10 Feb 2026) sets rules for the 2007 decree, extended to 31 Dec 2026. Obligations: adhesion at the Subdelegación, IDSE movements within 7 working days, monthly constancias, Buzón IMSS, joint liability for harvest contractors, loss of benefit on non-compliance. Correction: one source says it takes effect 180 days after publication, 8 Aug 2026, not on publication. That is now in force. IMSS, not the employer, computes the partial-exemption constancias, so the software job is thin. The relief ends 31 Dec 2026 unless extended, which makes it a one-year play. I found no specific competitor, but my search was shallow. Market size was not found; the datamx series is stale (2018). I could not read the primary text. Pain is moderate, buyers are scattered farms, and willingness to pay is uncertain.
